title: Psalm 7: Trusting in the Faithful God
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of Accusation
subpoints: David faces slander from Cush the Benjamite
The specific incident is not recorded in historical books
David appeals to God as the ultimate judge of his character

outline.title: The Nature of God: Yahweh Who Is
subpoints: God is the covenant-keeping God who does not change
The name Yahweh signifies eternal existence and immutability
Jesus Christ is the ultimate revelation of this faithful God

outline.title: God as the Believer's Refuge
subpoints: David takes refuge in God amidst persecution
Scriptural imagery of God as shield, hiding place, and high tower
The assurance that God remains faithful even when humans fail

outline.title: Security in Christ
subpoints: The New Testament view of being hidden in Christ and the Father
No power, including one's own sin, can separate believers from God's love
The assurance of divine protection for the church

summary:
In this afternoon sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro examines Psalm 7, a meditation by David in response to slanderous accusations from Cush the Benjamite. Although the specific incident is not detailed in the historical books of the Bible, the psalm reveals David’s urgent appeal to God for vindication and protection. The sermon highlights the theological significance of David addressing God as "Yahweh, my God," emphasizing that God is the covenant-keeping, immutable God who is "He Who Is." This eternal nature of God is fully revealed in Jesus Christ, who remains the same yesterday, today, and forever, providing a stable foundation for faith.

The message further explores the concept of God as the believer's refuge. Drawing on various psalms, it illustrates how God serves as a shield, hiding place, and high tower for those who trust in Him. This refuge is not merely a temporary escape but a permanent security rooted in God's unchanging character. Even when earthly relationships fail or personal sin feels overwhelming, God's faithfulness remains constant.

Finally, the sermon connects this Old Testament assurance to New Testament theology, noting that believers are hidden in Christ and the Father. Just as David found safety in God's presence, Christians today are assured that no power, including their own flesh, can separate them from the love of God in Christ Jesus. This provides profound comfort and confidence in the midst of life's trials and accusations.
